solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Power of nature regularly infusing calmness

indicators.note: infusing means being steeped into something, so the picked letters go inside the word for calmness

parts.note: calmness is cool, as in keeping one's cool

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word nature, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Nature's rhythms bring a calming, steadying power to the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the odd letters of 'nature' only; 'of' is a link, not part of the picked text.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and control are synonyms, both meaning authority or command over something.

clue.text: Wake up commander satisfied onslaught's beginning

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
met, as in met the requirements, means satisfied

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter of the word onslaught is taken

explanation.surface: A commander rouses himself, pleased that the attack has started.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round after sleep or unconsciousness is to wake up; the phrasal verb is a close synonym.

clue.text: Good old Grandma's first with a top tip for mother of kids

indicators.note: first means the word for grandma is placed before the letters for good and old

parts.note: nanny is a familiar word for a grandmother

indicators.note: tip means the first letter of the word top

explanation.surface: Granny was first at the scene, bearing a top tip for a young mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts NANNY ahead of G and O; 'tip' takes T from 'top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kids are young goats, so a female goat is literally the mother of kids, a playful definition.

clue.text: Check sulphur in tree sap

indicators.note: in means the sulphur symbol goes inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A test for sulphur content in the sap of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance exuded by pines and other trees, a kind of sap.

clue.text: Is unable to sleep before a funeral, makes up stories

indicators.note: before means the word for making up stories comes ahead of the funeral words

parts.note: to lie is to make up stories
a wake is a gathering held around a funeral

explanation.surface: Someone sleepless on the night before a funeral, inventing tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' reads as time, the eve of a funeral, but it places the stories in front of 'a funeral'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie awake is an idiom for staying in bed unable to fall asleep.

clue.text: Blathered on and escaped with a fine up front

indicators.note: up front means the with-a-fine letters go before the word for escaped

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
fled means escaped

explanation.surface: A prisoner talked endlessly and broke out, paying a fine in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' puts W, A and F ahead of FLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To waffle is to talk at length without substance, a synonym for blathering on.

clue.text: Broaden women's group study

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Broaden the scope of a women's group study.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a long-running British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden something is to make it wider; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Female artist knocked up advert about lifestyle overseas

indicators.note: knocked up in a down clue means the artist's letters are turned upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: about means the advert's letters go round the reworked life

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement
lifestyle splits as life plus style: the four letters of life, restyled into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman artist dashed off an advert about a lifestyle abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked up' turns the artist upwards in this down clue. 'lifestyle' does two jobs at once: 'life' is the fodder and 'style' tells you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Far afield means a long way from home, which suits being overseas, abroad.

clue.text: Relaxed look round Kent area

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
O is round in shape
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: A relaxed look around the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, so 'Kent area' gives SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and relaxed both describe something slack or not tight.

clue.text: Dying to go out with husband in boat …

indicators.note: to go out suggests the letters break out of their order, here those of dying and the husband letter

explanation.surface: A dying man, desperate to put out to sea with her husband in a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go out' rearranges DYING plus H. The ellipsis joins this clue to 14 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat, often for sailing or as a tender.

clue.text: Briefly contemplate eating at home with take away

indicators.note: eating means the shortened word surrounds the at-home letters
Briefly means the last letter of the word for contemplate is cut off

parts.note: to muse is to contemplate
in means at home

explanation.surface: Pausing to think about eating a takeaway at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take away' looks like a meal; it is subtraction. 'Briefly' drops the final E of the word for contemplate.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, minus means subtract, which is to take one number away from another.

clue.text: Said I had a blue quilt

indicators.note: Said means the words I had a, run together as I'd a, are spoken

parts.note: I had a, shortened to I'd a, is said like the name of the duck
down means sad, or blue

explanation.surface: Someone saying they once had a blue bedcover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' makes I'D A sound like EIDER, the duck.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick bed quilt, originally filled with the soft feathers of the eider duck.

clue.text: Make futile attempt to teach incoming Year 5 about current

indicators.note: incoming means what follows goes into the word for teach

parts.note: to train is to teach

indicators.note: about means the year and five letters go round the word for current

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
in means current or fashionable

explanation.surface: A teacher struggling to explain electric current to a Year 5 class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks electrical; it means in fashion. 'about' wraps Y and V round it, and 'incoming' sends YINV into the word for teach.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attempt something without success, a futile effort.

clue.text: Restored silence with fellow soldiers going on ahead

indicators.note: going on ahead means the fellow and soldiers letters are placed before the silence

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, army soldiers
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Peace is restored as a man and his troops march on ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a British Army corps, a stock crossword source for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling fresh is feeling revived and restored after rest.

clue.text: Seepage from great river reported

indicators.note: reported means the river name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the Great Ouse is a major river of eastern England

explanation.surface: Leakage from a big river, as reported in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Ouse is a long river in eastern England; 'reported' makes OUSE sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ooze is a slow trickle of liquid, which is what seepage means.

clue.text: … just even to have sex on board

indicators.note: on board means the word for sex is taken aboard, inside the word for even

parts.note: equable means even or steady
it is a crossword word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Continuing from 8 Down: a romance in a boat on an even keel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'merely'; it means fair. 'IT' for sex comes from old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and equitable both mean fair and impartial.

clue.text: Powerful one act play to include introduction from Hugh Grant

indicators.note: to include means the reworked letters surround the next part
play means the letters of one and act are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, followed by act as written

indicators.note: introduction from means the first letter of the word Hugh

parts.note: to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: A one-act play featuring a turn by the actor Hugh Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like the actor's surname; it means let. 'play' rearranges I and ACT into ATIC, which 'to include' wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes someone strong and muscular, so it is a synonym of powerful.

clue.text: Man found on grass after blow to head went to bed

indicators.note: after means the man-on-grass letters follow the blow
found on in a down clue means the man sits above the grass

parts.note: a hit is a blow

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word to

parts.note: he is a man
hay is dried grass

explanation.surface: A man was discovered on the lawn after being knocked on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow to head' reads as one injury, but 'to head' is the T alone. In a down clue 'found on' puts the man above the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going to sleep, a casual way of saying retired for the night.

clue.text: I don't understand Italy's best team getting demolished

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: getting demolished means the letters of best team are knocked down and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Italy's top football side being thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting demolished' rearranges BEST TEAM to follow I.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when something baffles you, meaning it is beyond your comprehension.

clue.text: Strongest Surrey opener's dismissed in cricket match

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the word Surrey
in means the word for dismissed goes inside the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
out means dismissed, as a batter is in cricket

explanation.surface: Surrey's opening batsman is out in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county with a cricket side; a Test is a full international cricket match, and a dismissed batter is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean sturdy and strong, so its superlative means the strongest.

clue.text: Former society girl and model makes commitment

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, was a young upper-class woman presented in society
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: An ex-debutante and model make a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' gives T from Ford's Model T car.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, an obligation or financial commitment.

clue.text: First Judy Blume novel's in stuff for charity shop

indicators.note: First means the opening letter of the name Judy
novel means new, so the surname is rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Judy Blume's first novel turns up in a charity shop's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges BLUME into UMBLE. A British jumble sale sells second-hand odds and ends for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumble is second-hand goods given away for resale, the sort of donated stuff a charity shop sells.

clue.text: Some nobility in priest's words of wisdom?

indicators.note: in means the nobleman goes inside the priest's letters

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest, with S for the possessive
an earl is one member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A noble among the sayings of a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EARL inside P and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls of wisdom are wise sayings, so the gems stand for wise words; the question mark flags the idiom.

clue.text: Not able to have posh new suit

parts.note: U means upper-class, or posh
to fit is to suit

explanation.surface: A man who can't afford a smart new suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means unsuitable or not capable, so it can stand for not able.

clue.text: Truth about terminal failure of plane

indicators.note: about means the word for truth goes round the final letter

parts.note: a fact is a truth

indicators.note: terminal means the last letter of the word failure

explanation.surface: The truth about why a plane crashed fatally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' takes E from 'failure'; 'about' puts it inside FACT. 'plane' looks like an aircraft; it is a flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one flat face of a cut gem, which is a plane surface.

clue.text: Drink plenty of water having drunk hearty red

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of hearty red are reeling and mixed up

explanation.surface: After too much robust red wine, drink lots of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges HEARTY RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehydrate is to restore lost body fluids, which means taking in plenty of water.

clue.text: Anger management class

indicators.note: management suggests the letters of anger are handled and reorganised

explanation.surface: A course of anger management sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management' rearranges ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a set or class of things of one kind, as in a product line.

clue.text: Evil spirit's trapped in hillside monastery

indicators.note: trapped in means the letters are held within the phrase hillside monastery

explanation.surface: A malevolent spirit is imprisoned in a monastery on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' picks the letters from hillsiDE MONastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil supernatural being, a devil or fiend.

clue.text: Where ordinary MPs are getting support by judiciary

parts.note: to back is to support
the bench means judges collectively, the judiciary

explanation.surface: Ordinary MPs win the support of the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK House of Commons, ordinary MPs without ministerial posts sit on the rear seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear seats in the Commons are where MPs without government or shadow posts sit.

clue.text: One's reluctant to spend one's energy seducing man

indicators.note: seducing means taking in, so the word for man surrounds the letters

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man
one's is read as one is: I for one, with an S for the shortened is
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone stingy putting their energy into wooing a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'One's' twice: once in the definition, once read as one is, giving IS. 'seducing' means taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is a person who hoards money and hates parting with it, reluctant to spend.

clue.text: Exceptional golden arches in Exeter building

indicators.note: building means the letters are assembled into a new structure

parts.note: the golden arches form the M logo of McDonald's

explanation.surface: A McDonald's sign looming over a building in Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges EXETER plus M. Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means far beyond the ordinary, so it fits exceptional.

clue.text: Finally, achy joints long gone and new heart in baseball team

indicators.note: Finally means only the last letter of the word achy
in means the heart letter is put inside the shortened joints
gone means the long letter has left the joints word

parts.note: ankles are joints

indicators.note: heart means the middle letter of the word new

explanation.surface: An ageing player with sore joints, his best days gone, gets a new heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes L from ANKLES to give ANKES; 'heart' takes E from 'new', and 'in' puts it inside. The New York Yankees are a famous US baseball club.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York team of that name is one of the best known in Major League Baseball.
